answer: Each identity claims one grid cell of a named island, locks an 80-credit bond, and files its sparrow nest count on a whisper beacon keyed to its identity. The auditor recomputes the count from the public census table and the beacon log: a wrong count, reused beacon ID, or claimed cell burns the bond. First filing 38, k-th 38+6(k-1), 1,000th 6,032; 1,000 fakes cost 3,035,000 plus 80,000 locked, each cell needing its own survey and beacon. A rented-nest ring fails: a replayed survey reuses its beacon ID and both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 38 once and reclaims the bond after a clean audit.
